stageLabel: The patent paperwork: a deadline and a corrected name
shapeSentences: An inventor facing a patent deadline completed paperwork, learned that the name on a form did not match the application and worked through a correction.
Finishing a form was not the end: a small administrative mismatch required another signed document.
Attorneys reported the correction, and the patent was granted later that summer; the record does not describe her private feelings.

facets.emotionalCore: Practical pressure from a deadline and a paperwork mismatch, without an invented account of panic or humiliation.
facets.decisionShape: Supplying the required affidavit and payment, then completing replacement paperwork after a name mismatch was reported.
facets.triggerEvent: Her attorneys warned that delay in the final paperwork could cost the patent; a later telegram identified a mismatched name.
facets.agencyState: She could sign forms and provide payment, while her attorneys arranged the certified copy, filing and correction.

biographicalFacts: Hedy Lamarr was twenty-seven during April–August 1942. On April 13 her attorneys warned that prompt attention to an affidavit and payment was needed to preserve her pending patent application. Their letter said the final government fee was due before May 13 and the affidavit had to precede payment by twenty days. On April 16 they forwarded an executed affidavit and acknowledged her check for the final fee. An April 18 telegram said the signature name differed from Hedy Kiesler Markey, the name on the application. A same-date request asked Charles Walton to obtain a new signature, and a covering letter reported enclosure of a properly executed form. That typed report is not a separately inspected replacement affidavit or proof of a known signing time. On August 11 Patent 2,292,387 was granted to Hedy Kiesler Markey and George Antheil. Its proposed system changed transmitter and receiver radio frequencies together to impede interference. The documented outcome is the grant of a patent.

beats.text:
Her name was Hedy Lamarr.

She was an actor who also helped invent a radio communication system.

Your life is not theirs.

But a piece of this story may still sit beside you.

You do not have to explain every part of yourself.

You are allowed to want your work taken seriously.
